speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed if the lesions have developed a central dimple or umbilication, and are they present on other parts of the body like the extremities or face?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the classic presentation of umbilicated pearly papules and the daycare exposure, this is highly suggestive of Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
